title: Scanner promotes exact hosts entries to suffix blocks
reproduction: Call scan_list_for_critical with only '0.0.0.0 whatsapp.net\n'. The embedded offline reproduction in tooling-audit-review.md invokes the actual functions without network.
expected: Only whatsapp.net is blocked by this exact hosts entry; suffix matching is reserved for formats with suffix semantics.
observed: Baseline: Seven domains are reported blocked, including mmg.whatsapp.net and static.whatsapp.net. extract_blocked_domains loses the rule kind and domain_is_blocked applies parent matching to every entry. Current: focused offline regression expectations pass.
fix: Separate exact hosts from suffix rules; use the current SourceLoader context-free ABP pattern; retain resolved raw_hits through report merging and treat historical hosts as exact. No new domain engine or additional syntax families.
test_evidence: Parser red: 8 methods ran with 12 failure events (7 failing methods; one passing control). Parser green: all 8 passed. Final suite: 33/33 passed; includes exact/plain/suffix/label-boundary/report-origin cases and a live-source constant/ABP-pattern drift guard. No app code executed.

title: Scanner silently misses valid hosts aliases and mixed-format entries
reproduction: Run actual scan_list_for_critical on five fixtures: 0.0.0.0 alias; 127.0.0.1 alias; ::1 host; indented IPv4 host; one unrelated hosts row followed by a plain critical domain. Exact fixture text is embedded in the review.
expected: mmg.whatsapp.net is recognized in all five forms accepted by the app hosts parser; reports must not classify these lists as clean.
observed: Baseline: All five fixtures produce no critical hits. The regex takes only the first host, excludes IPv6/leading whitespace, and one hosts row disables all plain-domain parsing. Current: focused offline regression expectations pass.
fix: Parse each line independently, trim whitespace and inline comments, consume every valid hosts alias, and accept the app's three blocking IP literals including ::1. Preserve mixed hosts/plain-domain input.
test_evidence: All five original alias/IPv6/whitespace/mixed subcases failed before the parser edit and passed after it. Comments/case/duplicate/malformed-alias controls also pass. Final 33-test offline suite passed without skips.

title: Scanner recommends unblocking domains it classifies as ads or telemetry
reproduction: Mock one downloaded list containing only ads.telegram.org and crashlogs.whatsapp.net, clear historical known results, capture all open(...,'w') calls in StringIO, and run actual main.
expected: No compatibility allowlist additions for explicitly NONE/LOW telemetry-only hits; retain ad/tracker blocks and recommend only justified exact compatibility hosts.
observed: Baseline: high_risk_lists is empty, but recommendations contain ads.telegram.org, crashlogs.whatsapp.net, *.telegram.org and *.whatsapp.net. Markdown also tells users to add all unprotected domains. Current: focused offline regression expectations pass.
fix: Generate exact recommendations only from unprotected positive-impact hits. Remove parent/wildcard expansion and old broad-unblocking Markdown; JSON and Markdown use the same filtered set while ads/telemetry remain visible as blocked evidence.
test_evidence: Four advice tests failed before this edit and then passed. Final controls include empty input, telemetry-only input, mixed compatibility/telemetry, suffix-derived hits and already-allowed hosts. Scanner main is executed with downloads mocked and all three writes captured in memory.

title: Certificate helper deletes unrelated caller-directory files before validation
reproduction: Static reproduction: the first command is rm localhost.*; glob-match localhost.backup and localhost.notes. From repository root ssl.conf is absent although Resources/certificate/ssl.conf exists. Do not execute the original against real data.
expected: Only explicitly selected certificate outputs may be replaced after configuration/tool success; caller working directory and unrelated localhost.* files remain untouched.
observed: Baseline: An unqualified broad removal runs first in the caller directory. OpenSSL then resolves ssl.conf from that same directory, so a root-directory invocation can delete matching files and fail to generate replacements. Current: focused offline regression expectations pass.
fix: Anchor config and exact localhost.crt/key outputs to helper directory; prevalidate regular outputs; use umask 077, private same-filesystem staging and a cooperative lock; publish only complete successful generation; roll back ordinary publish failures and clean only explicit owned paths.
test_evidence: Copied baseline helper: 8 methods exposed 15 assertion failures and one missing-fixture error. Updated helper: all 14 mocked-OpenSSL tests pass, including foreign CWD/spaces, unrelated files, failures/incomplete/empty output, first-time generation, second-rename rollback, private key mode, symlinks/directories and lock preservation. bash -n and ShellCheck pass. No real OpenSSL or repository helper execution; no power-loss/SIGKILL atomic-pair claim.

title: Both translation configurations reference four removed source resources
reproduction: Parse all source_file entries in both configurations and test local existence. Missing: values/strings_support.xml and raw/help_faq.html, raw/help_problems.html, raw/help_s_on_s_off.html under app/src/main/res/.
expected: Every configured source resource exists, or a retired resource is explicitly removed from both sync configurations.
observed: Baseline: Both independent configurations contain 23 resources and the same four absent source paths; those source entries cannot be read for translation sync. Current: focused offline regression expectations pass.
fix: Remove exactly the four retired source resources in both configurations without changing remaining resource/language mappings. A shared offline guard parses INI/YAML, checks existence and compares all remaining source/filter/language/format entries.
test_evidence: Before edit both configurations had 23 sources and four missing paths; source-existence and expected-retained-count checks failed. After edit both have 19 existing sources with matching mappings; both tests pass. No remote Transifex call or resource-content edits.

title: Contributor quickstart invokes a release build without required trust inputs
reproduction: Follow the documented fresh-contributor sequence with SDK configured but without signingStoreLocation/signingStorePassword/signingKeyAlias/signingKeyPassword/updateManifestPublicKeyBase64/releaseSigningCertificateSha256. The final command is ./gradlew assembleRelease.
expected: The basic contributor quickstart builds using a debug key; production release instructions explicitly supply or link the mandatory trust inputs.
observed: Baseline: app/build.gradle:80-127 recognizes assembleRelease as a release request and throws when signing properties are absent, then requires the update key and signer hash. The quickstart provides none. Current: focused offline regression expectations pass.
fix: Make assembleDebug the first contributor build command, qualify debug-key behavior when release properties are absent, and link RELEASING.md for signed builds and mandatory trust inputs. No build guard or dependency changed.
test_evidence: Debug-first and release-guide-link tests both failed before the documentation edit and both pass now. app/build.gradle SHA256 remains a0a6c117c82bcdb74a4257fb38531349600d53a6f82468b909bf2cd2688166fe. No Gradle invocation; main owns integration review.
